# Alex Cronin

> Alex Cronin is a technologist and entrepreneur. He runs Hardware Nation, the IT infrastructure company he started in 2006, and spent two years (2024 to 2026) building Nanites AI, a system of AI agents that troubleshoot network problems. He works across technology from silicon to software, and AI most of all.

## About

- Came to the United States from Russia at the end of July 1991, at age nine, weeks before the failed August coup against Gorbachev, and grew up in Atlanta. His parents arrived without a dollar and took odd jobs for about a year, then his father started several businesses (including a travel agency, a local Russian newspaper and a passport-renewal service). As a teenager he translated between Russian and English for them, and later took those businesses online.
- Has sold door to door, on eBay and office to office.
- Graduated from Georgia Tech. Started Hardware Nation in 2006, at 24, and built it without outside funding. Over 20 years he has built relationships with hundreds of manufacturers, ODMs, software companies, customers and investors, and brought in hundreds of engineers, mostly as contractors.
- He built hardwarenation.com himself, with hundreds of thousands of products online, backed by warehouses across the country.
- Hardware Nation helps organizations buy, build and run IT infrastructure. It has served more than 1,000 customers, from startups to global enterprises, universities and government agencies. It began working with Edgecore in 2016.
- His deployment experience includes Arista, HPE (including Juniper), NVIDIA switches running Cumulus Linux, and Edgecore switches running SONiC, including SONiC in enterprise production networks.
- Today he builds AI workflows and multi-agent systems at Hardware Nation.
- Built Nanites AI largely self-funded and tested it in labs. It was named an emerging Agentic NetOps vendor in Gartner research, covered by InformationWeek, included in Cisco DevNet's discussion of commercial AI agents for networking, and was one of 12 finalists (from more than 400 applicants) in the 2025 T Challenge run by T-Mobile US and Deutsche Telekom.
- In 2026, his view is that as engineers use general AI tools like Claude Code and Codex directly on networks, a network-specific harness matters more. It needs to be built and tested for each device, operating system and firmware version, so wrong actions are stopped before they reach the device. Each new model generation needs the harness re-engineered and re-tested.
- Has presented Nanites at Deutsche Telekom's headquarters in Bonn, Germany, to both Deutsche Telekom and T-Mobile US. Has also been a speaker at CableLabs events and at Network X Americas events. Takes part in OCP, ONUG and NANOG.
- His interests include understanding human nature, deep tech from silicon to software, business and technology books, space, physics (especially quantum mechanics), aviation, geopolitics, economics, markets and venture capital.

## Pages

- [The Hardware Nation story](https://cronin.ai/hardware-nation/) covers what 20 years of Hardware Nation taught him, including building it online, open networking and working directly with ODMs, supply chain, and where the business fits as AI changes the market.
- [The Nanites story](https://cronin.ai/nanites/) covers what two years of building an AI network engineer taught him, with four lessons from building it and a dated timeline.
- [Engineering an Agentic Network Operations Platform](https://cronin.ai/papers/engineering-an-agentic-network-operations-platform.pdf) is his preprint (September 2026) on findings from nearly two years of development, laboratory evaluation and field use, drawn from 914 captured investigations, 118 alert-driven runs and five focused experiments.
